result.title: Editing as Language: Teaching LLM Agents a Grammar for Native Context Editing
result.summary: A synopsis in novels folds a story into a few lines; a function in code gathers many steps with a single execution. Context editing is native to language itself. In this paper, we propose the Native Context Editing (NCE) framework, which gives language model agents a grammar for natively editing their own context. By encoding context-editing operations in a grammar of dedicated special tokens, we teach the agents to invoke edits through the language itself. We train agents on iteratively constructed trajectory segments, with each teacher edit conditioned on the evolving context. This establishes context editing as an atomic and inherent capability of LLM agents, enabling them to dynamically modify their context as they generate responses over long-horizon reasoning and interaction. Compared with context-editing methods that learn to generate tool-use code within specific external harness environments, our approach integrates context editing as an internal mechanism of the model's native generation process, enabling better generalization across diverse real-world workflows. On four long-horizon agentic benchmarks (Terminal-Bench 2.0, SWE-bench Verified, SWE-bench Multilingual, and SWE-bench Pro), NCE improves the average task success rate over the base model by 5.6 percentage points for LongCat-Flash-Lite-Sparse and by 4.5 for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, while reducing average token usage by 36% and 15%, respectively.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Native Context Editing（NCE）框架，用一组专用特殊 token 构成「语法」把上下文编辑操作写入语言本身，并以迭代构建的轨迹片段（教师在演化上下文上给出编辑）训练 LLM agent 在长程推理与交互中自行修改上下文；在四个长程 agent 基准上提升成功率并显著减少 token 消耗。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽属纯文本 agent 工作，不涉及视觉输入，但把「状态修改」内化为模型原生生成能力、并以演化上下文上的教师编辑做轨迹级监督，可能与 LVR 的 latent 状态更新、控制 token 化与贡献分配/轨迹监督训练可供核查。
